fields.name: Rāmacandra Khān (Benāpola)
fields.notes: Born Śāntidhara, a Śrotriya Rāḍhīya brāhmaṇa; zamindār near Benāpola and childhood friend of Hussain Shah. Sent a prostitute to Haridāsa Ṭhākura; had Caṇḍī's pavilion scraped and washed after Nityānanda sat there; then the king's wazir looted and imprisoned him (CC Antya 3.101-102, 156-160). Not Rāmacandra Khān of Chatrabhoga (#1246).

fields.name: Rāmagopāla dāsa (Rasa-kalpavallī)
fields.works: Rasa-kalpavallī (12 sections, 1595 Śaka / 1673); Śrī Narahari-śākhā-nirṇaya; Śrī Raghunandana-śākhā-nirṇaya; padas
fields.notes: Disciple of Ratikānta Ṭhākura (#1308) of Raghunandana's family; younger son of Śyāmarāya, of the line of Cakrapāṇi Caudhurī of Śrīkhaṇḍa (Cakrapāṇi → Nityānanda → Gaṅgārāma → Śyāmarāya); his brother Madana put the Govinda-līlāmṛta into Bengali verse. A renowned Vaiṣṇava poet.

fields.name: Kṛṣṇadāsa Guñjamālī
fields.place: Born at Lahore; Govardhana; Multān, Gujarat, Olambā (Punjab): his Deities; Sindh; Vṛndāvana (end of his life)
fields.disciples: Banwāricandra (his nephew, mahānta at Multān); Janārdana Vipra (#591, mahānta at Olambā)
fields.notes: Born at Lahore; at seventeen came to Gopāla of Govardhana; surrendered to Lord Caitanya in Vṛndāvana, who gave him His guñjā-mālā; by His order installed Deities at Multān, in Gujarat and at Olambā (Baḍa Gauḍīya Gaddī); preached the holy name in the Punjab and Sindh; ended his life in Vṛndāvana. Not Kṛṣṇadāsa (Rāmadāsa) Kapūra #750.
